title: Why Lottery Winners Go Broke So Fast
hook_text: THE OBLIGATION SPIRAL DESTROYS LOTTERY WINNERS

beats.say: Most lottery winners are broke 5 years later, not because of sports cars, but due to an obligation spiral.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary silhouette standing on a rain-slick concrete bridge at blue hour under sodium streetlights.

beats.say: You see a $20,000,000 jackpot and think financial freedom is finally locked in for good.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a rusted iron fire escape cutting across a cold concrete wall, lit by harsh fluorescent light.

beats.say: Where does all that cash actually vanish to so quickly?
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of heavy iron padlocks on a weathered gate under a dark overcast sky.

beats.say: Most folks assume poor budgeting or luxury shopping drains the bank account.
beats.visual: High angle shot of a wet asphalt highway intersection with no traffic, dimly lit by a single distant amber light.

beats.say: The real culprit is a hidden psychological trap that forces you to fund everyone else's life.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person walking away down a long concrete underpass cut by harsh shadows.

beats.say: When a relative asks for $5,000 to save their home, saying no feels impossible.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of rough concrete pillars dripping with rainwater under a cold highway overpass.

beats.say: How do dozens of sudden requests drain a multi-million dollar fund in just 60 months?
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a massive steel industrial crane tower cutting into a dark, foggy sky.

beats.say: Every accepted favor creates three new demands from friends and distant family members.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of dark ocean waves crashing against jagged black rocks at night.

beats.say: The obligation spiral swallows principal faster than any sports car ever could.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a lone figure standing at the edge of a vast, empty rooftop against a navy blue horizon.

beats.say: Wealth isn't destroyed by what you buy yourself, but by what you say yes to for others.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of wet cobblestone street reflecting a single harsh sodium light.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a heavy steel bridge structure disappearing into thick evening fog.

caption: Why winning millions often leads straight back to zero. #moneypk #personalfinance #wealth #psychology #moneyrules
description: An exploration of the obligation spiral that drains lottery windfalls within five years.
first_comment: What's the hardest person to say no to when money gets tight?

facts.claim: Most lottery winners face severe financial distress or bankruptcy within five years.
facts.basis: Documented studies by the National Endowment for Financial Education and financial planners regarding sudden wealth syndrome.

loop_map.stakes: A $20,000,000 lottery jackpot and the illusion of permanent financial freedom.
loop_map.big_question: Where does all that cash actually vanish to so quickly?
loop_map.assume: Most folks assume poor budgeting or luxury shopping drains the bank account.
loop_map.reveal: The real culprit is the obligation spiral of funding everyone else.
